desk.headline: Adjusted EPS up 17% to $4.66, beat; $900m FTC charge cut revenue 1% to $8.9bn; cautious Q4 outlook on Middle East
results: Room nights grew 7% and gross bookings 10% to $54.5bn; adjusted revenue rose 9% to $9.8bn.
Reported revenue fell 1% to $8.9bn after a $900m reduction, plus a $100m accrued loss, linked to an FTC matter involving Priceline.
Adjusted EPS rose 17% to $4.66, helped by a lower share count; GAAP EPS rose 7% to $3.61. Figures reflect April's 25-for-1 share split.
Adjusted EBITDA margin held at 47.0%; adjusted fixed costs grew 6%.
$2.1bn of shares bought back in the quarter ($12.4bn authorisation left); $0.42 dividend payable 31 Dec 2026.

guidance.summary: Booking still expects high single-digit growth in 2026 bookings, adjusted revenue and adjusted EBITDA, and low-to-mid-teens adjusted EPS growth. Q4 is guided much softer, assuming Middle East disruption lasts to year-end.

items.metric: Gross bookings / adjusted revenue / adjusted EBITDA growth

points: Global demand eased late in the quarter as international travel softened; domestic and shorter trips held up.
The CFO called the Q4 travel backdrop "mixed", citing the Middle East conflict, higher airfares and unrest in some European cities.
AI tools are an early positive: users of Priceline's and Agoda's assistants convert at about twice the rate of other users.
Cost programme on track for $650m of yearly savings by 2027, but Q4 carries extra spending on flights, attractions, dining and AI.
Priceline is negotiating with the FTC; no settlement has been reached and the company's filing flags possible restitution and penalties above $1bn.
